Saved. Summary of what I learned and recorded:

The error was a Gini coefficient normalization trap. With exactly 2 values (total receipts vs total expenditures), I got 0.006 vs the gold 0.012 — exactly half. The digits were all correct; only the denominator convention was wrong.

Root cause: OfficeQA's gold uses the **sample** mean-absolute-difference form (denominator n(n−1)), while I used the **population** form (denominator n²), which yields exactly (n−1)/n of the gold — for n=2 that's half.

Concrete rule saved: for n=2, Gini = |a−b| / (a+b) — absolute difference over the sum, no extra ÷2. General small-n: MAD/(2·μ) with MAD summed over n(n−1), not n².

Recorded in:
- New reference: references/gini-coefficient-small-n.md (closed form, worked example, the "excluding investments" row guidance, surplus/deficit sign check, output format)
- Pointer line in SKILL.md
- One compact memory entry for cross-session recall

This is generalizable — any future OfficeQA Gini question over a small extracted set will hit the same denominator fork.
